prompts.text: Which everyday custom makes you feel most welcomed when visiting someone else's home?
Describe someone showing you hospitality in a way you hadn't encountered before.
Learn how your host prepares a favourite drink or hear why they chose a particular family tradition?
You invite someone over from a different upbringing. What would you ask to make the visit comfortable?
People have very different ideas about what makes a home welcoming.
Being a considerate guest starts with asking instead of assuming.
What is a small courtesy you remember from someone you met only once?
Recall learning an unfamiliar greeting at a gathering and appreciating the reason behind it.
We are invited to two celebrations with different etiquette. How could we prepare without overthinking it?
Compare our favourite welcome rituals or the customs we find hardest to explain?
Which question helps you understand how someone approaches friendship?
Tell me about meeting somebody whose idea of loyalty challenged your assumptions.
Ask what makes a person a dependable friend or what makes a friendship enjoyable?
A new acquaintance tells you they prefer a small social circle. What might you want to understand about that?
People often use the word friendship for relationships with very different levels of closeness.
A small circle of friends isn't necessarily a sign of disinterest in meeting new people.
How do you usually know when an acquaintance has become a friend?
Describe a time someone you knew casually showed unexpected reliability.
We both describe our oldest friendships. What could the differences tell us about how we connect?
Talk about a friendship that lasted through change or one that began in an unusual way?
What's a topic you enjoy exploring with someone who has read different books from you?
Recall a discussion where someone explained a story you'd understood in a completely different way.
Find out which ideas a person has changed their mind about or which ones they're still exploring?
We're each given the same short article and asked what stood out. What differences would you expect?
Two people can encounter identical information and notice very different details.
Being willing to rethink an idea is a more interesting quality than having an opinion ready about everything.
Which subject would you enjoy researching alongside a person you have just met?
Tell me about somebody who made a difficult subject feel approachable through conversation.
We discover a shared interest in a topic but disagree on where to start learning. How should we choose?
Explore a local history question together or compare explanations of an everyday scientific mystery?
What social habit has been easiest to understand after hearing its cultural background?
Describe seeing a familiar gesture used with a completely different meaning.
Learn the story behind a traditional greeting or the reason for a community celebration?
We're planning a gathering for people with different dietary customs. What should we ask without making assumptions?
A custom can seem strange from a distance and practical once someone explains its origins.
Respectful curiosity is often more useful than pretending to understand every tradition.
What's one tradition you enjoy even though you don't practise it yourself?
Recall a conversation that changed how you interpreted a celebration or ritual.
A new friend asks why your family prepares for an event in a particular way. How would you explain it?
Hear an elder tell a tradition's origin or see a younger person's modern interpretation?
How does someone show that they're comfortable with a conversation becoming more personal?
Recall somebody changing the topic gracefully when you weren't ready to discuss something.
Ask permission before a sensitive question or wait for the other person to bring it up?
We're having a lively discussion that unexpectedly touches a difficult memory. What would be a considerate next response?
Trust often grows when people discover they can decline a question without upsetting the other person.
Curiosity is valuable only when it leaves room for privacy.
What's a signal you use when you'd rather keep a story for another day?
Describe someone understanding a boundary you hadn't found easy to explain.
A person we've just met starts sharing more than the setting allows. How could we respond with care?
A conversation that develops slowly over several meetings or one with clear questions about comfort levels?
Which kind of collaboration teaches you most about another person's character?
Tell me about completing a small project with someone whose working style surprised you.
Plan an event together or solve a practical problem as a team?
We volunteer at a community event but have completely different strengths. How might we allocate tasks?
People reveal patience through how they respond when a plan needs adjusting.
A person admitting a mistake can be more reassuring than someone never appearing uncertain.
What does a good teammate do when somebody else has a better idea?
Recall a stranger stepping in to help without expecting anything in return.
We need to agree on a plan quickly, and neither person wants to dominate. Which question would you ask first?
Work with someone who prepares carefully or someone who adapts easily when circumstances change?
What's an ordinary habit that tells you something about how a person spends their free time?
Describe learning about an unexpected creative hobby during a casual conversation.
Ask what a person has made recently or what they like spending time observing?
We're invited to show an object connected to a pastime. What would you choose to reveal about yours?
People sometimes talk more openly about their routines than about their ambitions.
An interest doesn't need to be productive to be worth discussing.
Which hobby has helped you connect with someone whose background was very different from yours?
Recall watching somebody turn an everyday object into something unexpectedly beautiful.
A new friend invites you to join an activity you find intimidating. What might make trying it easier?
Compare collections we've kept over the years or the skills we've learnt purely for enjoyment?
What helps you understand what another person finds funny without relying on stereotypes?
Tell me about a joke you didn't understand until someone explained the situation behind it.
Discuss the funniest everyday misunderstanding we've seen or compare our favourite styles of comedy?
We're watching a comedy from a different country and keep laughing at different moments. What would you ask me?
A shared sense of humour can emerge through storytelling even when cultural references differ.
Someone who can explain a joke kindly is more enjoyable company than someone who mocks confusion.
What style of humour do you appreciate more now than you did a few years ago?
Recall a person using a gentle joke to make a tense moment feel less awkward.
We have to choose one short, family-friendly comedy clip to introduce someone to our tastes. What's your criterion?
Compare amusing stories from real life or explore the humour in old sayings?
What's something you notice about the way a person maintains long-distance relationships?
Describe a chance encounter that turned into an occasional but lasting connection.
Stay in touch through shared articles or set aside time for a regular call?
We've met at a conference and live in different cities. What would be a natural reason to reconnect?
Some connections become meaningful through infrequent conversations that pick up smoothly.
A good first meeting doesn't oblige either person to promise a lifelong friendship.
What would make you comfortable accepting an invitation from someone you have only met once?
Recall reaching out to a new acquaintance months later and finding the conversation surprisingly easy.
We share a mutual interest and want to stay connected without endless messaging. What could we agree on?
Exchange an occasional recommendation or arrange a relaxed visit when we're in the same area?
Which quality do you admire most when you see someone mentoring a younger person?
Tell me about receiving guidance from somebody you initially knew only through work.
Learn from someone who asks probing questions or one who demonstrates their skills patiently?
We both volunteer to guide students at an event. How would we explain our different career journeys?
Good mentors often share uncertainty as well as lessons from their successes.
A person's willingness to teach says more about them than their professional title.
What do you find most valuable in advice from someone at a different life stage?
Recall a colleague who made a complicated task feel less intimidating.
A new connection asks for an introduction to your field. What would you explain first?
Discuss a lesson learnt from making mistakes or a skill you'd like to pass on to somebody else?
